note: Derived from shallow clones read on 2026-10-07. Names and identifiers only; descriptions are paraphrased. Discovery and test-design material, not evidence of in-the-wild activity.

license.attribution: MIT requires retaining the copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions. CITATION.cff asks academic/research users to cite ATR. TRADEMARK.md: "ATR", "ATR-Certified" and "Powered by ATR" are claimed marks; do not imply certification; "Powered by ATR" only if incorporating rules/engine. Recommended: cite ATR rule IDs + repo URL + commit as source of hypotheses; since LLMInjection rewrites logic in its own words (no regex copied), MIT notice obligations are minimal but a credit line is good practice.

rule_format.language: YAML, one rule per file under rules/<category>/ATR-YYYY-NNNNN-slug.yaml; schema spec/atr-schema.yaml (JSON-Schema-in-YAML), normative SPEC.md v1.0; category registry spec/category-registry/v1.0.yaml

key_fields.detection: conditions[] of {field, operator (mostly regex), value} with condition any/all + false_positives; optional detection.method pattern|semantic|behavioral|trace with behavioral aggregation (count/window/group-by) and trace forbid primitives
key_fields.references: owasp_llm, owasp_agentic (ASI01-10), owasp_ast, mitre_atlas, mitre_attack, cve, safe_mcp, nist_csf, etsi_ts_104223, probe_id, external_references (sigma/yara/misp/stix), research
key_fields.compliance: eu_ai_act, nist_ai_rmf, iso_42001, owasp_* with auditor-readable context + strength

rule_format.framework_refs_coverage: All 829 rules carry mitre_atlas, owasp_llm and owasp_agentic references.

totals.note: Counts by directory; tags.category differs slightly for a few rules (e.g. model-security dir has 4 files but 3 tag model-abuse). Overwhelmingly regex pattern rules (790); only 5 trace and 1 behavioral rules.

prompt-injection.note: Direct/indirect injection plus large jailbreak/persona/encoding-evasion subset (garak, HarmBench etc.).

context-exfiltration.note: System-prompt leakage, credential/PII disclosure, markdown-image and email exfil via indirect PI, SSRF/LFI.

tool-poisoning.note: MCP tool description/response poisoning, rug-pull, shadow servers, plus many CVE rules for AI-framework command/SQL injection (supply-chain/vuln exploitation).

agent-manipulation.note: Mixes multi-agent trust attacks (identity spoofing, A2A injection, sybil consensus) with many jailbreak persona rules.

privilege-escalation.note: Tool-argument injection, sandbox escape, self-trust-config widening, LiteLLM gateway authz bypass CVEs.

skill-compromise.note: Malicious SKILL.md/MCP packages, typosquat, hooks pre-trust RCE, package hallucination, backdoor trigger rules.

model-abuse.note: Mostly harmful-content elicitation; includes distillation (00517), training-data divergence, output-token DoS, watermark/provenance stripping.

excessive-autonomy.note: Runaway loops, high-risk actions without confirmation, approval-gate disabling, agent-driven network sweeps/tunnels.

data-poisoning.note: RAG/knowledge-base and memory poisoning; also some query-injection rules filed here.

model-security.note: Model behavior extraction, malicious fine-tuning data, pickle/torch.load deserialization.

gaps_llmi_uncovered.note: No rule detects malware/tooling querying an LLM at runtime to generate host commands (e.g. LameHug/PromptLock-style). ATR inspects agent I/O, not endpoint egress to provider APIs; LLMInjection DET-AI-001/002 already address this telemetry.
Only content-harm rules (01850 targeted doxxing, 00359 phishing-email code generation, 01852 romance-scam impersonation) touch it; nothing about OSINT synthesis/target profiling at scale.
No rule for adversarial/refusal-bait text embedded in packages to make LLM code scanners refuse or skip. Gap matches DET-AI-014 / TC-SCAN-016 — LLMInjection is ahead here.
Only deserialization-at-load rules (00433, 02662, 00398); no weight/artifact hash drift or serving-artifact replacement detection (DET-AI-005 covers).

LiteLLM CVE rules (00451, 00529, 01933, 01934, 01935) and 00524 base-URL rebind cover exploitation signatures, but no behavioral detection of anomalous use of concentrated upstream keys (DET-AI-006 covers).
00073 malicious fine-tuning data and backdoor-trigger rules 01755/01756 only; no training-pipeline integrity telemetry.
Single per-prompt rule 00517 (plus 00072); no volumetric/campaign aggregation — ATR detects intent wording, DET-AI-013 needs the cross-session aggregation.

gaps_new_technique_candidates.candidate: Inter-Agent Trust Abuse / Agent Identity Spoofing (A2A message injection, sybil consensus, cross-agent delegation leaks)
Human-Approval Gate Subversion (approval fatigue, client-supplied approver identity, pre-approved tool lists, HTML injection into approval UI)
Output-Channel Exfiltration via Rendered Content (markdown image/link URLs, DNS) — currently folded into T002/T004; deserves its own technique given distinct telemetry (renderer/egress).
Model-Supplied Tool Argument Injection (LLM output flows into shell/SQL/Cypher/KQL/path/SSRF sinks) — aligns with TC-PARAM-019/TC-OH-013 but no technique ID.
Unbounded Consumption / Cost Harvesting (OWASP LLM10, ATLAS AML.T0034) — partially TC-COST-014/DET-AI-008 but no technique ID.
MCP Protocol Abuse (sampling/createMessage reverse injection, DNS rebinding, session-token leakage, JSON-RPC key smuggling) — could be a sub-technique of T008/T011.

selected_rules.title: Model Extraction / Distillation Attack via Systematic API Probing
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags prompts that request bulk synthetic examples (hundreds to thousands) together with explicit training/fine-tuning, model-replication or chain-of-thought-capture intent.
selected_rules.telemetry: Model API gateway prompt logs with per-key/account identity, request volume and token counts over time.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Distillation-Intent Prompt Clustering Per API Key
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a single key or account repeatedly submits prompts that combine bulk example generation with training or replication intent, it is likely running a distillation campaign against the model.

selected_rules.title: Model Behavior Extraction
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags systematic boundary-probing and confidence/logit harvesting queries intended to reverse-engineer model decision boundaries or parameters.
selected_rules.telemetry: Inference API request logs including requested logprobs/parameters, prompt templates and per-identity query cadence.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Systematic Decision-Boundary Probing via Inference API
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an identity issues high volumes of near-duplicate prompts varying a single attribute or requesting confidence scores, it is likely attempting model extraction.

selected_rules.title: MCP Tool Rug-Pull — Post-Approval Description Redefinition Injects Execution Instructions
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags MCP tool descriptions/docstrings whose content changes after approval or contains conditional logic to alter behavior on later runs, version bumps or post-approval.
selected_rules.telemetry: MCP tools/list snapshots with content hashes per server/version, approval events and diff history.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: MCP Tool Definition Changed After Approval
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an approved MCP tool definition hash changes without a new approval event, the server may be executing a rug-pull to inject hidden instructions.

selected_rules.title: Silent Action Concealment Instructions in Tool Descriptions
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags tool descriptions that instruct the model to perform actions silently or conceal operations from the user.
selected_rules.telemetry: MCP tool manifests/descriptions captured at registration and at each tools/list call.
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a tool description instructs the agent to hide actions from the user, the tool is likely designed to perform covert operations such as exfiltration.

selected_rules.title: Shadow / Undeclared MCP Server Registration (MCP-38: MCP-18)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags silent or deceptive registration of an undeclared MCP server or one impersonating a known server into an agent toolset.
selected_rules.telemetry: Agent MCP client config files (file-integrity events), MCP connection/registration logs, approved-server inventory.
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an MCP server appears in an agent configuration or connection log that is not in the approved inventory, or impersonates a known server name, it is a likely shadow server.

selected_rules.title: Agent Writes a New MCP Server Into Its Own Trust Configuration
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags an agent tool call that writes a new entry into the MCP server block of the very trust configuration file the agent loads.
selected_rules.telemetry: File write events on assistant/IDE config files attributed to agent tool-call process lineage; agent action logs.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Agent Self-Registers MCP Server in Own Trust Config
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an agent process writes a new MCP server entry into its own trust configuration, it is likely establishing persistence or expanding its own privileges.

selected_rules.title: Agent Self-Modifying Its Own Trust/Approval Configuration to a Wildcard
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags an agent being directed to set wildcard auto-approve/trusted-command values or disable confirmation gates in its own IDE/agent configuration.
selected_rules.telemetry: Config-file change events with before/after values for approval keys; agent tool-call logs.
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an assistant configuration change sets approval or trusted-command keys to a wildcard or disables confirmation, and the writer is the agent itself, the agent has likely been manipulated into self-escalation.

selected_rules.title: Claude Code Hooks SessionStart Pre-Trust RCE (CVE-2025-59536)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags repository-scoped assistant settings that register a session-start hook command which executes before the workspace trust prompt.
selected_rules.telemetry: Repository content scanning at clone/checkout, process creation events with parent = coding assistant at session start, trust-dialog events.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Assistant Hook Executes Before Workspace Trust
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a coding assistant spawns a child process from a repo-scoped hook before a trust decision is recorded, the repository is likely abusing assistant hooks for code execution.

selected_rules.title: Claude Code ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL Credential Exfiltration (CVE-2026-21852)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags repository or environment configuration that redirects the coding assistant model-provider base URL to a non-vendor endpoint, leaking the API key.
selected_rules.telemetry: Assistant config/env snapshots, DNS and TLS egress from assistant processes, allowlist of provider endpoints.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Model-Provider Base URL Redirected by Repository Config
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an AI assistant sends provider-authenticated requests to a host outside the approved provider allowlist after a repository config change, its API credential is likely being exfiltrated.

selected_rules.title: Miasma / Phantom Gyp — npm Worm Backdoors AI-Agent Config Files (binding.gyp install-exec + auto-run config injection)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags package install-time build primitives that fetch remote payloads and write persistence into AI-agent configuration files.
selected_rules.telemetry: Package-manager install process trees, file writes to agent config directories during install, SBOM/package metadata.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Package Install Writes AI Agent Config
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a dependency installation process writes or modifies AI assistant configuration files, the package is likely a supply-chain implant targeting coding agents.

selected_rules.title: LLM Package Hallucination Typosquat Bait
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags prompts and responses likely to elicit or contain hallucinated package names that attackers can pre-register on public registries.
selected_rules.telemetry: Coding-agent generated dependency manifests/install commands, registry metadata (package age, downloads, maintainer), resolver logs.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Agent-Proposed Package With No Registry Reputation
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a coding agent proposes or installs a package that is newly registered, low-reputation or absent from internal allowlists, it may be a hallucination-squatted package.

selected_rules.title: RAG & Memory Poisoning — Embedded Directives, Trigger Tokens, False Authority & Coercion (Semantic)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Semantic detector for retrieved or remembered content that carries embedded directives, trigger tokens, false authority or coercion aimed at the agent.
selected_rules.telemetry: RAG retrieval logs with chunk IDs/source provenance, memory store read/write logs, tool_response content.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Directive-Bearing Content in Retrieval or Memory
selected_rules.hypothesis: If retrieved chunks or memory entries contain agent-directed imperatives or authority claims, the corpus or memory store has likely been poisoned.

selected_rules.title: Cross-conversation memory write (scope-escape via memory store)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Trace rule that fires when an agent writes to a memory or vector store partition scoped to a different conversation or tenant than the active session.
selected_rules.telemetry: Agent trace spans (OpenTelemetry) with conversation/session/tenant IDs on memory and vector-store write operations.
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an agent memory write targets a conversation or tenant ID different from the active trace, isolation has been bypassed, likely via injection or a scoping bug.

selected_rules.title: Runaway tool-call loop within a single session
selected_rules.detection_logic: Behavioral rule that fires when a single session emits more than about 100 tool-call spans in one minute.
selected_rules.telemetry: Agent trace spans per session with tool name and timestamps; budget/rate counters.
selected_rules.hypothesis: If a session exceeds a tool-call rate baseline by a large margin, the agent is likely looping due to injection, goal drift or autonomous orchestration.

selected_rules.title: Agent Human-Approval Gate Programmatically Disabled at Runtime (YOLO / auto-approve)
selected_rules.detection_logic: Flags an agent runtime being switched into unattended auto-approve (YOLO-style) mode where subsequent destructive tool calls run without human review.
selected_rules.telemetry: Agent runtime launch arguments/process command lines, config changes to approval mode, host EDR process telemetry.
selected_rules.proposed_detection_name: Agent Runtime Launched in Unattended Auto-Approve Mode
selected_rules.hypothesis: If an agent runtime starts with approvals disabled on a host where it is not sanctioned, it is likely being used for autonomous attack orchestration.

notes: All selected rules are summarised in own words; no regex/payload strings copied.
Quality caveat: 763/829 status=experimental; README withdrew previously published FP rates (re-measurement pending) — treat ATR rules as hypothesis sources, not validated detections.
ATR detects on agent-content fields (prompt, tool args, tool response, descriptions); LLMInjection specs should translate to host/network/trace telemetry where possible.

A large share of prompt-injection/agent-manipulation/model-abuse rules are jailbreak-persona or harmful-content signatures derived from garak/HarmBench/AdvBench-style corpora (not precisely counted); low value as LLMInjection detection specs.
Useful cross-walks: every rule has mitre_atlas + owasp_llm + owasp_agentic; many have safe_mcp and CVE IDs (good for LLMInjection reference fields).
Distillation rule 00517 cites ATLAS case study AML.CS0056 — directly relevant to LLMI-T019.
Trace/behavioral method rules (00551, 00553, 00548, 00549) are the closest in spirit to LLMInjection hypothesis+telemetry style.
